terminology.note: Changed the ambiguous Complex Real Integrals title to Computing Real Integrals. Distinguished isolated/removable/essential singularities from poles, ordinary improper integrals from principal values, primitive/antiderivative from a definite integral, and a chosen logarithm branch from a multivalued expression. Used a dedicated English Cauchy-theorem link and matching Taylor/Euler links.

mathematics.note: Checked all 17 display formulas after normalizing Res/留数 labels; read the Cauchy-theorem annotation separately. Verified positive piecewise C1 simple-contour hypotheses, finite interior isolated singularities, none on the curve, and winding-number qualification. Checked R>1/R>a bounds, absolute convergence, k>0 exponential decay, the Jordan estimate, and 0<a<1 keyhole endpoint convergence. On 0<arg z<2π, checked lower-side e^(-2πia), reverse orientation, residue e^(-πia), and the resulting phase equation and π/sin(πa). Source supplementary calculations check four semicircles, three small-circle pole integrals and five logarithmically transformed real integrals; numerical evidence is illustrative, not proof. Explicitly checked that the principal part is the sum of negative-power terms, not the coefficient collection.
